alalal-c45559-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 9: whether God's being in someone by grace is being in them simply or only in a qualified sense.

alalal-c45559-d1e115.summary: Introduces the question on Lombard's statement that God dwells in the saints, in whom he is by grace.

alalal-c45559-d1e127.summary: First argument: being in by grace is being in simply and being in by essence only qualifiedly, since to dwell is to remain simply, and not dwelling means remaining only in a qualified way.

alalal-c45559-d1e146.summary: Second argument: where someone dwells he remains; so where God does not dwell he would pass through, and God would pass through those in whom he is only by essence, presence and power.

alalal-c45559-d1e162.summary: Contrary argument: being and well-being relate as simple and qualified; by essence, presence and power God gives being, by grace well-being, so presence by essence would be simple and presence by grace qualified.

alalal-c45559-d1e188.summary: Solution: being in by grace is being in simply and in a nobler way.
claims: God's indwelling by grace is a simple and nobler mode of presence.

alalal-c45559-d1e197.summary: Reply to the first argument: presence by grace presupposes common presence and perfects it on the side of the creature being perfected, not on the side of God who perfects.
claims: Grace presupposes and perfects God's common presence, from the creature's side only.

alalal-c45559-d1e210.summary: Reply to the second argument: the dwelling implied by grace is not opposed to passing through, but is named from the rest of the will it effects, since grace makes the will of the saints remain and rest in God, which common presence does not do.
claims: Indwelling is named from the will's rest in God that grace produces.

alalal-c45559-d1e228.summary: Reply to the contrary argument: common presence gives only natural being, which is not the best completion, so presence by grace is better. Yet common presence is not presence in a qualified sense: both are presence simply, though they connote unequally good effects.
claims: Both common presence and presence by grace are presence simpliciter, differing in the goodness of their effects.

alalal-c45559.summary: Article 9 asks whether God's presence in the saints by grace is presence simply or only in a qualified sense, given that God's common presence gives being and grace gives well-being. Albert holds that presence by grace is presence simply, and nobler. It presupposes and perfects God's common presence on the side of the creature, not of God. 'Dwelling' is named from the rest of the will in God that grace produces. Common presence, which gives only natural being, is also presence simply; the two differ in the goodness of the effects they connote.
claims: God's presence by grace is presence simply and in a nobler way than his common presence.
Grace perfects common presence from the creature's side, without change in God.
Indwelling is named from the rest of the will in God that grace effects.
